headline: 5 Coast Guard vessels renamed, removing names of 4 national leaders
summary: Vessels previously named after 1971 Liberation War leaders and the slogan 'Joy Bangla' have been renamed after naval personnel who died in the line of duty.
details: The government has approved the renaming of four Bangladesh Coast Guard (BCG) vessels that were named after national leaders who played pivotal roles in the 1971 Liberation War.
Another vessel, BCGS Joy Bangla, has been renamed BCGS Adomya Bangla.
The decision was communicated via a Home Ministry letter issued shortly after Jail Killing Day, which commemorates the assassination of the four national leaders in 1975.

The vessels previously named after Syed Nazrul, Tajuddin, Mansur Ali, and Qamaruzzaman have been renamed BCGS Firoz Kabir, BCGS Nurul Islam, BCGS M Humayun Kabir, and BCGS Ashraf Siddiqui respectively.
According to the Coast Guard, the new names belong to naval personnel who lost their lives during operations, encounters with pirates, or while performing duties in dangerous conditions.
Firoz Kabir was a lieutenant commander who died during a severe storm in the Sundarbans. Nurul Islam and Ashraf Siddiqui were killed during anti-smuggling operations.
M Humayun Kabir was a sailor who died in 2006 while fighting pirates in the Sundarbans. The Home Ministry did not provide a specific reason for the name changes.

headline: Two DGFI members dismissed and jailed in extortion case
summary: Sergeant Al Mamun and Lance Corporal Md Nuruzzaman were sentenced to one year in prison following a court martial for assaulting and extorting a businessman.
details: Two members of the Directorate General of Forces Intelligence (DGFI) have been dismissed from service and sentenced to one year in prison each following a court martial.
The convicts, Sergeant Al Mamun and Lance Corporal Md Nuruzzaman, were arrested on October 25 after an alleged extortion attempt on a motorcycle trader named Mohammad Sharif.
According to the case forwarding report, Sharif was confined in a flat in Chandrima Model Town, Mohammadpur, and demanded to pay Tk 10 lakh.
The victim had already handed over Tk 70,000 before being assaulted and threatened further.
The victim escaped by spotting a police patrol vehicle at a tea stall in Shyamoli around 3:00 am on October 25.
Police arrested six people, including the two DGFI personnel, and seized the car used in the crime.
The two DGFI members were handed over to the army and tried under military law, where the allegations against them were proved.
caption:
Two DGFI members have been dismissed and sentenced to one year in prison for extorting a businessman.

Two members of the Directorate General of Forces Intelligence (DGFI) have been dismissed from service and sentenced to one year in prison each following a court martial.

The convicts, Sergeant Al Mamun and Lance Corporal Md Nuruzzaman, were arrested on October 25 after an alleged extortion attempt on a motorcycle trader named Mohammad Sharif.

According to the case forwarding report, Sharif was confined in a flat in Chandrima Model Town, Mohammadpur, and demanded to pay Tk 10 lakh.

The victim had already handed over Tk 70,000 before being assaulted and threatened further.

The victim escaped by spotting a police patrol vehicle at a tea stall in Shyamoli around 3:00 am on October 25.

Police arrested six people, including the two DGFI personnel, and seized the car used in the crime.

The two DGFI members were handed over to the army and tried under military law, where the allegations against them were proved.
